notes: Metric is Abs(observed - reference) / Abs(X), not ordinary absolute error: the scaled Gamma inverse computes [LogProbability + LogGamma1p(Shape)] / Shape, so this quantity IS the relative error of the quantile it produces. Scored as ordinary absolute error the contract would be unfailable - 8.0E-27 against a 5E-16 threshold at X = 1E-13. The fitting set understated the worst error and placed it in the interior; the independent holdout extended coverage to the lower contract boundary and found 1.917E-16 at X = 1E-307 against 1.363E-16 on the fitting grid. The strict 2E-16 therefore gives only 1.04x and is rejected; 5E-16 gives 2.61x. The seam neighbourhood is excluded rather than merely unmeasured: those three points are owned by LogGamma1p.series_seam, and the promoted small rows end at X = 0.24.

Ownership and classification, not a numerical promise: deliberately carries no threshold, because a number here would read as a frozen claim. The point one ulp ABOVE the seam runs the delegated PROB_LogGamma route and inherits that kernel's error, roughly two orders above the series floor - measured 2.24E-14 at 0.25 + 1 ulp against 4.31E-17 at 0.25, a step of 5.68E-14 across the seam. Pooling the two sides into the small contract would either loosen it 100x or fail the seam for no reason. Freezing a seam threshold would need its own disjoint holdout and a defined seam metric.
